note: Draft course model for the prototype. Modules 1-6 follow the proposal's description of the course; Modules 7-8 are PLACEHOLDERS and must be replaced with the real syllabus before demoing to the instructor.

modules.title: What is Emerging Technology and Innovation
objectives: Explain why AI is a general-purpose technology

concepts.name: Sustaining vs. disruptive innovation
concepts.description: Sustaining innovations improve existing products for current customers; disruptive innovations start in low-end or new markets with simpler, cheaper offerings and move upmarket (Christensen).

misconceptions.text: Disruptive simply means a radically better or more advanced technology

concepts.name: AI as a general-purpose technology
concepts.description: General-purpose technologies (electricity, the internet, AI) spread across many sectors and enable complementary innovations.

modules.title: Problem Framing and the Science of Innovation
objectives: Reframe a problem before solving it
Use statistical process control to separate signal from noise

concepts.name: Problem reframing
concepts.description: Restating a problem precisely (who, why it matters, current limits) before choosing a solution.

concepts.name: Falsifiability (Popper)
concepts.description: A claim is scientific only if it could be shown false; set success criteria before testing.

concepts.name: Statistical process control
concepts.description: Control charts separate common-cause variation from special-cause signals that exceed control limits.

modules.title: The Nature of Technology (Arthur)
objectives: Describe technology as a combination of components harnessing phenomena
Place a technology on Arthur's maturity arc

concepts.name: Arthur's principles: combination and phenomena
concepts.description: Technologies are combinations of existing components that harness natural phenomena to meet a need; new technologies come from combining old ones.

concepts.name: Technology maturity arc
concepts.description: Technologies move from origination through development and adaptation to maturity and lock-in.

modules.title: Innovation by Imitation
objectives: Apply Adopt-Transform-Apply to a workplace problem

concepts.name: Adopt-Transform-Apply (Lift-Shift-Drop)
concepts.description: Find a proven solution in another domain (adopt/lift), adapt it to the new context (transform/shift), and implement it (apply/drop).

concepts.name: Displacement of concepts (Schon)
concepts.description: New ideas arise when a concept from one context is displaced into another and reinterpreted.

modules.title: Invention vs. Innovation
objectives: Classify innovations as incremental or breakthrough

concepts.name: Invention vs. innovation
concepts.description: An invention is a new idea or device; an innovation is the successful application of an idea that creates value in practice.

misconceptions.text: Invention and innovation are the same thing

concepts.name: Incremental vs. breakthrough innovation
concepts.description: Incremental innovations improve existing things step by step; breakthrough innovations create new categories.

modules.title: Diffusion and Adoption
objectives: Describe Rogers' adopter categories and five attributes
Locate the chasm and explain why it matters

concepts.name: Rogers' diffusion of innovations
concepts.description: Adopter categories (innovators 2.5%, early adopters 13.5%, early majority 34%, late majority 34%, laggards 16%) and five attributes: relative advantage, compatibility, complexity, trialability, observability.

concepts.name: Crossing the chasm
concepts.description: The chasm sits between early adopters and the early majority, at roughly the 16% point of the adoption curve (2.5% innovators + 13.5% early adopters).

misconceptions.text: The chasm is between the early majority and the late majority

modules.title: [PLACEHOLDER] Responsible AI and Governance
objectives: Apply the NIST AI RMF functions
Identify privacy obligations such as FERPA

concepts.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
concepts.description: Four functions: govern, map, measure, manage.

concepts.name: Privacy and FERPA
concepts.description: Education records are protected; access is limited to school officials with a legitimate educational interest.

modules.title: [PLACEHOLDER] Proof of Concept to Proof of Value
objectives: Distinguish proof of concept from proof of value
Design a 90-day pilot with success metrics

concepts.name: Proof of concept vs. proof of value
concepts.description: A proof of concept shows something can work; a proof of value shows it delivers measurable value in a real setting.

concepts.name: 90-day pilot and success metrics
concepts.description: A time-boxed pilot with value measures defined up front and a go/no-go decision point.
